conclusions: Headless contact remains slow without rendering, so GUI is not the primary reason for the contact deficit.
At 400Hz each physics step has a 2.5ms real-time budget; latest approach/close/belt-finish need5.387/7.508/10.241ms.
Latest whole-loop RTF0.986 hides400Hz-contact aggregateRTF0.398 and worst belt-finishRTF0.244.
Newton iterations rise in contact phases; latest mean approach1.097, close4.304, belt-finish7.939. Older vsdense totals were effectivelyequal, so earlier slowdown was not iteration inflation.

Native dense-hessian capacity fallback=0; fixedCSR guard healthy. Old profiles locate real GPU dynamics/constraint/line-search work, but cannot identify the unique bottleneck of the final configuration.
Compressed NPZ save and MP4 rendering occur outside the measured physics loop; device trace writes, batch readbacks and monitoring remain inside, and their exact final share is not isolated.
150Hz/200Hz earlier trials violated1mm validity. Lowering Hz or simplifying model changes the validation premise and is not a demonstrated solution to this goal.

next_concrete_change.limitations: Hit rate is currently unknown; elliptic cone curvature may change each iteration. Even eliminating all400x400 factors is not demonstrated to supply the required3–4x worst-contact speedup.
